x: Among the middle-distance men, Len Marchant and Willie Nankeville were very much to the fore, and with John Brown and Vic Blowfield showing great promise, we can look forward with confidence to next season.

This was a most regrettable omission and we give our apologies to Briggs, who is now serving in the Army, and is stationed at Larkhill. Victor Blowfield is showing international form over the country. His winning of the Club Ten was magnificent.

Dick Towndrow, making one of his rare appearances in our colours, was a good winner of the scratch race, followed by Vic Blowfield, who in his first attempt at cross-country racing, certainly surprised many by his forward running.
As winners of the race last season, we thus had to find a new scoring team, and our hopes received a set-back when Vic Blowfield failed to arrive in time.

Vic Blowfield ran excellently to finish second, and continues to show great promise in his first season over the country. Scoring six aside in the four-club match, resulted thus—Thames Valley H. 45 points, Belgrave H. 59, Surrey A.C. 114, Metropolitan Police 256.

Over the last two miles or so Herbert went away in fine style to win from Vic Blowfield with Frank Abberton a strong third. These three were followed closely by Tom Carter and Bert Footer, Bert managing to beat Tom in a sprint down the finishing straight.

He ran an excellent race to work his way through the field, and although Vic Blowfield hung closely on his heels, Derrick finished a good second to Len Marchant, the winner, with a yard or two to spare from Vic Blowfield, who was third.
Running for Middlesex were Vic Blowfield, who had dropped out of the County race owing to shoe trouble, and Geoff Pearson, while George Lucas was in Kent colours, and A.
At the halfway stage Arthur Penny and Vic Blowfield were running together with the rest of the field strung out in this order—Pearson, Frost, Eales, Tobin, Stokell.

Len Marchant, Vic Blowfield, Albert Frost, Jack Brown and Eric Herbert all gained standard awards, and with the men we have available I think we could take on any club in the country, at say 6 or 8 × 1 mile.

The rest of the field had a good tussle for second place with Vic Blowfield proving the stronger over young Arthur Bruce. Alan Sexton scored a double by winning the 300 yards, off 14, with a new member in R.

Vic Blowfield won the 1 mile and so far Wandsworth had had the first two home in every running event. Bill Sutton was second to Dave Grigg in the Discus Throw, and then Ted Read won the 220 yards and the home team also won the medley relay.

With Bill Lucas, Ted Stimpson (who was a 1939 international over the country), Vic Blowfield, Albert Frost, and last but by no means least, Len Herbert (who represented England in last year's International race), we have the men who can sweep the board as regards the “ open ” races, and, given a fai…

Even so, they only won by the narrow margin of 5 points, and Vic Blowfield and Albert Frost again ran extremely well. We were also the holders of the “ Odling-Smee ” Cup, awarded to the first club to finish their team of 12 men, but owing to Bert Footer's retirement, only had 11 in the first 93 plac…

Vic Blowfield led almost throughout and finished a comfortable winner from Albert Frost and Bill Lucas. George Lucas unfortunately had to retire with leg trouble and Len Herbert was away competing in the International race in Paris.
Albert Frost then took our “ A ” team into the lead, which Vic Blowfield kept, although going slightly off the course, which enabled the Birchfield man to get close on his heels.

Bill Lucas won the 1 mile, and Len Marchant ran away with the 880 with Vic Blowfield in second place. Our 2 milers suffered a shock when Turing of Walton went away in the final lap to win in 10 mins. dead.
Les Grimshaw finished second in the 100 yards, but pulled a muscle in the 220 and this trouble has kept him off the track since then. Vic Blowfield was third in the 880 and E.
Vic Blowfield and Derrick Burfitt also picked up useful points in the 1 mile event, and our team also won the team race in the 2 miles race.
Len Marchant won the 880 in 2 min. 2.9 secs., and Vic Blowfield won the 1 mile in 4 min. 37 secs. Bob Wise finished second in the 440 with Jim Beaumont third, but the final scores saw us well behind

Lockyer, a new member, ran well to finish second in the 880 yards, and Vic Blowfield gained third place in the 1 mile. George Lucas lost a close race by inches in the Kent County 3 miles race in record time, and Charlie Melchior won the Javelin Throw in the Hertfordshire event.
Vic. Blowfield, second, and Tommy Clinton, fifth, ran exceptionally well and were both chosen for Middlesex in the Inter Counties C.C.

Coming to the scratch race, this was won by Vic Blowfield with Dick Towndrow second and Ted Stimpson third. To beat the half-hour over our course is quite good running, so it can be seen that Vic put in some really fast running, which should gain him many honours before the season is over.
The placings in our club five miles were repeated with Vic Blowfield once again leading the field home. Scoring six aside the team result was: Belgrave H. 28 points, Oxford University 50 points.

Len Herbert, the holder, was defending his title, but in a fast run race he was beaten on the run-in by Vic Blowfield. Dick Towndrow gained his first club championship award in being third, with a past-holder in Arthur Penny fourth, and Tom Clinton fifth.

A good field of 32 runners faced the starter, including the holder Vic Blowfield, while Len Herbert and Tom Carter, 1946 winner, and Arthur Penny, winner in 1934, 1936, 1938 and 1939, also turned out.
The senior race was over a 10 miles course and from the start Sydney Wooderson went in front followed by Vic Blowfield, with Ted Stimpson also well up.

…nce again Sydney Wooderson was up the front but this time there was a small bunch of runners with him including our own Vic Blowfield. On the last lap Wooderson made his effort but Vic kept with him stride for stride and then about half-a-mile from the finish Vic made a gallant attempt to get away f…

Birchfield had a good four running for them and although Vic Blowfield gave us the lead on the first leg, which Ted Stimpson maintained on the second stage, Bill Lucas had to give way to Reeves of Birchfield and Bobby Reid went off with a good lead from George Lucas for the last lap.

Vic Blowfield and Len Herbert were notable absentees but Ted Stimpson ran a good race to beat George Lucas with both Archie Bedford and Eddie Short causing rather a surprise by their forward positions.
At the half-distance Vic Blowfield and Frank Abberton were together in the lead with Bill Lucas and Len Marchant fairly handy, but the rest of the field were already well strung out.

Rather naturally there were new names in our team in Vic Blowfield, George Lucas, Stan Eales, Eric Herbert and Albert Frost. It is interesting to note that of our ten runners, six were past or future Internationals.

His challenger was none other than our own Vic Blowfield who was always up with the leaders, and when they came round for the last of the three large laps, Blowfield and Wooderson were together with Shorrocks of Hailesowen some 25 yards behind in 3rd place.

This however did fall once again to LEN HERBERT (6th); and other members of our team on this most difficult day were :- DICK TOBIN 31, VIC BLOWFIELD 37, TED STIMPSON (this years President - none other) 51, STAN EALES 65.

…rs; returning to form to take the European 5,000 meters in 1946 and then in the twilight of his career, to pass our own Vic Blowfield in the last 400 yard of the 1948 National Cross-Country Championships to achieve another memorable victory.…

He achieved his objective after a tremendous struggle with our own Vic Blowfield, only taking the lead in the finishing funnel. Belgrave won the team race with 154 points beating their conquerors of 1947, Sutton Harriers by 20 points.
Our performers in Middlesex under the name of Cadogan AC slipped to 4th team, only Derek Burfitt, 9th, and Vic Blowfield, 10th, making the county team.
As winners of the race last season we thus had to find a new scoring team, and our hopes received a set-back when Vic Blowfield failed to arrive in time.

Our positions were as follows:- 3 V.S.Blowfield 56:46; 4 E.S.Stimpson 57:24; 7 L.W.Herbert 57:50; 10 F.J.Abberton 58:05; 15 T.P.Clinton 58:20; 36 C.T.Carter 60:01; 38 C.L.Stokell 60:05; 65 R.W.Tobin 61:37; 84 S.R.Eales 62:25; 90 A.E.Frost 62:50; 106 A.F.Mitchell 63:28; 132 G.M.Pearson 64:15.
He was contemporary with Arthur Penny, Bert Footer, Vic Blowfield, Ted Stimpson, Charlie Smart, Harry Shields, Len Marchant, Bill Lucas, my brother Len and many others.
1948 · Aylesford · V.S. “Vic” Blowfield · 3rd

He placed second, only the third Belgravian in our history to do so (the others being Vic Blowfield in 1948 and Allen Graffin in 2002. Birhan Dagne has won the women’s race and Kassa Tadesse the junior men’s race – but we patiently wait for a senior men’s winner!
For only the third time since we first contested this race in 1920, our leading man was placed 2nd – Vic Blowfield in 1948, Allen Graffin in 2002 and now 23 year-old Phil Wicks.
